proof.criterion: A hub whose grant predates session consumers degrades safely (INFRA-514 architect's round question 1)
proof.surface: A real envoy-listener process on a real nats-server whose NATS user carries exactly the listener grant before this change (`listenerGrantBeforeSessionConsumers()`), with a session stand-in
proof.observed: Both PASS (0.39s and 0.50s). The listener starts, does not refuse, and answers every registration that asks for a consumer with `mode: core, reason: no_grant`; it logs 'the NATS user may not manage session consumers; sessions stay on core delivery until the grant carries them' exactly once per ten-minute episode (noGrantBackoff, packages/envoy/cmd/listener/session_delivery.go:47-51); the session entry records no consumer delivery; and the message still reaches the session on its core subscription with the stored copy acknowledged `skipped`, as before this change. A grant that carries the consumer API but not `$JS.API.CONSUMER.LIST.ENVOY_NOTIFICATIONS` costs one consumer info per session at a restart and logs once (session_relay.go:503-519). Nothing is dropped silently in either case. The deploy step the grant needs: an `envoy-infra` plugin release and a `pulumi up`, which makes a new instance template and so replaces the VM of every hub with a `listener`, a `machineId` or a `dispatchMachineId` user, once, with NATS down from the old VM's stop until the new VM's `nats` unit starts (packages/envoy/infra/docs/nats-hub.md, 'Updating a hub', which this change updates), then the new VM's `listener API hosts:` boot line is checked; INFRA-14 carries it at INFRA-553's replacement or a later live reload.
proof.negativeControl: The old grant itself is the broken input: the same registration body that is answered `consumer` on the full grant is answered `core`/`no_grant` on `listenerGrantBeforeSessionConsumers()`, and the listener keeps serving.
